compressed_items.content: Adaptive Permeability: A Dynamical Theory of System Survival Under Changing Environments.
Dynamical theory of system survival under changing environments.
Complex-system failure is framed as self-revision failing to keep pace with changing constraints, not inability to achieve goals.

Adaptive survival is proposed to depend on effective revision capacity relative to environmental-change velocity; survival requires reality-coupled adaptive-capacity generation to outpace changing required constraints.
K_eff,t = kappa_t C_rev,t.
C_rev,t is revision capacity; kappa_t is the permeability coefficient measuring the degree to which external reality influences internal revision.
Capacity without coupling is inert; rapid internal change can remain disconnected from the environment that determines usefulness.
Lambda_t = dot(K_eff,t)/v_req,t = dot(kappa_t C_rev,t)/dot(X*_t).
dot(K_eff,t) is the rate of generating effective adaptive capacity; v_req,t = dot(X*_t) is the velocity of changing environmental requirements.

Three regimes are defined conceptually: surplus means adaptive-capacity generation outpaces constraint change; critical tracking matches environmental velocity; debt means environmental change exceeds restructuring ability.
Adaptive surplus Lambda_t>1; critical tracking Lambda_t=1; adaptive debt Lambda_t<1.
Surplus is stated to increase resilience; critical tracking permits survival without margin; debt may temporarily function through reserves while accumulating structural debt.
Current performance is a lagging indicator and may remain high while adaptive ability is deteriorating.
Psi_t = kappa_t d/dt(1/tau_a); decreasing tau_a corresponds to the positive direction and increasing tau_a to the negative direction described by the source.
tau_a is adaptation latency: time required to recover after an environmental perturbation.
Decreasing adaptation latency is interpreted as faster future-shock recovery; increasing latency as accumulating structural friction.
A_t = integral_0^t exp[-lambda(t-tau)] Psi_tau d tau.
lambda represents obsolescence.
Past adaptations lose value when they cease to match current reality.
A resilient system is stated to require continuous generation of new adaptive capital.
Adaptive capacity is bounded rather than capable of unlimited growth.
dot(K_eff,t) <= B_adapt,t; the source identifies v_req > dot(K_eff) as environmental velocity exceeding the adaptive-production limit.
B_adapt represents available computational, energetic, organizational, or biological resources.
When environmental velocity exceeds the production limit, the system is stated to inevitably enter Lambda<1.
APE is specified to test whether the invariant predicts future resilience using three agents under identical resource constraints.
APE control statements: N_params = constant and C_compute = constant.

Agent A learns current tasks without restructuring its adaptation mechanism; Agent B has an adaptive substrate for discovering improved revision pathways; Agent C produces high internal change velocity with low environmental coupling.
APE predicts Psi_A≈0, Psi_B>0, and for Agent C v_rev increases while kappa decreases, leading to Psi_C<0.
All agents may initially achieve similar performance: R_A≈R_B≈R_C.
Environmental acceleration alpha = d v_req/dt.
Evaluate future recovery under increasing environmental acceleration; falsify the theory if positive adaptation velocity fails to predict improved recovery under unseen future shocks.
Predicted future recovery-latency ordering: tau_future,B < tau_future,A < tau_future,C.
Positive adaptation-velocity condition used in the falsification statement: Psi_t>0.
Intelligence is defined not as solving today's environment but as becoming structurally harder to defeat by tomorrow's environment.
Adaptive systems are defined by reality-coupled capacity generated while changing, rather than amount of change alone.
Core formalism leaves kappa scale/estimation, C_rev measurement, X*_t state-space/metric, Lambda normalization/commensurability, and sufficient K_eff dynamics unspecified.
Psi operationalization remains incomplete because kappa has no measurement protocol and tau_a has no perturbation/recovery-threshold/aggregation protocol.
The obsolescence parameter lacks units/estimator and B_adapt lacks a common measurement scale across heterogeneous resource types.
APE leaves resource-equivalence operationalization, executable agent mechanisms/parameterization, and v_rev definition unspecified.
The source does not define R performance, explicitly relate tau_future to tau_a, or specify the environmental-acceleration/unseen-shock schedule.
